Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES June 3, 2021

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on
June 3, 2021 via Zoom. Commissioner Denmon (Chairman) called the meeting to
order at 6:05 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Lee Denmon, Commissioner at Large (Chairman)
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District Two
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore, District Three
  Commissioner Christopher Beck, District Four
  Sabrina Barnes, Director - Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Teresa Estrada, Superintendent- Parks
  Gilbert Gonzalez, Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Geoffrey Okamoto, Transportation Operations Manager
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Henry Brown

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  NONE

Staff Report

1. Staff report recommending the Parks and Recreation Commission recommend
  the Mayor and Council Members approve payment in the amount of $16,622.23
  to L.A. Business Printing Services for additional work required for publication
  of the Community Information Guide.

  Commissioner McLemore made a motion to approve the recommendation
and Commissioner Denmon seconded. The motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, Beck and Denmon
  Nays: None

2. Staff report recommending the Parks and Recreation Commission recommend
  the Mayor and Council Members approve payment in the amount of $9,130.00

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES June 3, 2021

  to Sculpture Conservation Studio for emergency conservation services for the
  Inglewood War Memorial (obelisk) located at City Hall South Mall.

  Commissioner Beck made a motion to approve the recommendation and
Commissioner Fragoso seconded. The motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, Beck and Denmon
  Nays: None

Verbal Comments

  Gilbert Gonzalez gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks Administration
for both Park Maintenance and Graffiti regarding the following:

Park Maintenance
   The Park Maintenance staff has returned to work, effective June 1, 2021.
  Staff is working full force with a goal of ensuring all due diligence is met.
   Beginning Monday, June 7, 2021, staff will be replacing all signage
  located at the Parks
Graffiti:
    The month of May experienced a spike of graffiti in District 4 in the Darby Dixon
  and surrounding areas.
    North Park located in District 2 also had increased activity outside the
  men’s restroom and at the water treatment area/building.
    Edward Vincent Park continues to be heavily tagged.
    Any and all reports of graffiti can be made on the Graffiti hotline (310)
  412-8739.

Commissioner Beck asked if an update was available on the graffiti report
previously given on May 6, 2021 at the Parks and Recreation Commission meeting
which indicated there was tagging and vandalism of private property - homes and
cars. Mr. Gonzalez stated from information provided by the Inglewood Police
Department, the concentration of graffiti previously reported was due to a rival
gang member relocating into the community, the individual tagged the area thus
prompting retaliation activity resulting in an increase of additional tagging at the
time. It can be considered an isolated incident with current activity in a decline.

Commissioner Beck thanked Mr. Gonzalez. Director Barnes asked Mr. Gonzalez
to inform the Commissioners on graffiti deployment in the areas. Mr. Gonzalez
informed Commissioners that there are two full-time graffiti abatement staff
members assigned per district working both during the week and weekends with
additional part time staff, resulting in staff being available 7 days a week.

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES June 3, 2021

Commissioner Denmon asked regarding the picnic tables located at Center Park
in District four (4), is the abatement team responsible for the removal of that graffiti.
Mr. Gonzalez answered yes. Both Commissioner Denmon and Commissioner
Beck thanked Mr. Gonzalez.

Teresa Estrada introduced the Sports Recreation Supervisor Anthony Harris.
Mr. Harris began with the city a year ago starting right at the beginning of the stay
at home order. He comes to us with an extensive background in sports. Mr. Harris
oversees Edward Vincent, North and Queen Park. Mr. Harris spoke to everyone
present. Ms. Estrada stated recruitment for a supervisor for Rogers Park is
currently open. Due to the vacate position, Mr. Harris is also currently overseeing
Rogers, Ashwood and Siminski Park.

Teresa Estrada gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding
the following:

Summer Updates

June marks the summer for our Recreation Division. We are happy to report that
many of our outdoor amenities will reopen. This includes:
   Vincent Park Swimming Complex
   Summer Day Camp (Darby and Rogers)
   Dodgers RBI (Reviving Baseball in Inner Cities)

RBI Baseball

We have again partnered with the Los Angeles Dodgers Foundation and will be
serving 450 kids at Rogers, Darby and Edward Vincent Park. RBI Baseball will
begin in two (2) weeks.

Summer Day Camp

Summer Day Camp begins June 21, 2021 and ends August 18, 2021, lasting a
total of eight weeks. Camp consists of four sessions. Day Camp will be subject
Los Angeles County health and safety guidelines. Capacity still remains at half -
serving 50 kids at Rogers Park and 40 kids at Darby Park. Session One is
completely filled; Sessions Two, Three, and Four have a few slots remaining.
Summer Camp serves kids, ages 3-12. Session Two will begin July 5, 2021.

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES June 3, 2021

Swimming Pool Complex

The Swimming Pool Complex opens Wednesday, June 16, 2021 and closes Labor
Day, Monday, September 6, 2021. Youth swim sessions are completely full with
the exception of the 9:30 am start time. Encourage neighbors, family and friends
to register as again classes are filling up quickly. Adult and Parent and Me classes
are filled to capacity. We will be serving at 60% of our usually capacity – 50 kids.
Additional information can be found by visiting the Department’s website.

Family Paint Day

Family Paint Day is something new. It’s an activity where family and youth as
young as age five come and paint together in the park. The class will be held on
June 19, 2021 at Edward Vincent Park. Currently, five seats are available for the
June 19 class. Another session will be held on July 24, 2021 at Darby Park. The
cost is $10.00 per person Classes are an hour and a half beginning at 12:30 pm
and ending at 2:00 pm. An instructor will be there to assist. All families paint the
same subject and are allowed to take their masterpiece home.

Movies in the Park

Movies in the Park will return at Edward Vincent Park on July 17, 2021 and July
31, 2021. Movies are typically Disney Classics and or Disney Films. Movies will
be shown in a drive in setting in the parking lot near the multi-purpose fields. Movie
goers will remain in their cars. The cost is $15.00 per vehicle. Registration can be
completed online at parksrec.cityofinglewood.org. Commissioner Beck
commented that during the previous Commission meeting (May), Ms. Estrada was
excited about opening in person camp and implementing more arts and crafts
activities and that it’s good to see that both goals were attained and filled capacity
quickly. Commissioner beck stated that hopefully after June 15, 2021, less
restrictions allowing more participants will be available. Commissioner Beck
thanked both Ms. Estrada and Mr. Harris and also welcomed Mr. Harris onboard.
Geoffrey Okamoto gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division
regarding the following:

    The Senior Transportation Program continues to provide senior trips to
  dialysis and critical doctors’ appointments. Drivers, as well as patrons, are
  required to wear face coverings and practice safe social distancing during
  transport.

    Drivers are currently being scheduled to also transport seniors and other
  persons with disabilities to other needed appointments.

  4
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES June 3, 2021

  The Transportation Section is currently conducting regular safety meetings,
  with discussions held on the aspects of safety and other relevant topics.

  Our Elderly Nutrition Program continues to provide daily freshly cooked
  meals, weekly produce and monthly shelf-stable emergency meals to its
  490 participants enrolled in the program.

  Summer Food Summer Program (SFSP) Grab “N” Go will commence at the
  City’s parks and local library, Monday through Friday, from June 14, 2021,
  through August 20, 2021, Breakfast will be provided from 9:00 AM to 11:00
  AM, and lunch and snacks will be served together from 12:00 PM to 2:00
  PM at the following sites.

  o  Darby Park
  o  Rogers Park
  o  Siminski Park
  o  Lockhaven Community Center
  o  Ashwood Park
  o  Edward Vincent Park
  o  Crenshaw-Imperial Library

  The Inglewood Senior Center is closed due to the Pandemic. Calls
  regarding from both local seniors and observers the Senior Center’s
  Reopening are being handled by Center staff who continue to provide
  ongoing assistance during these challenging times. Commissioner Denmon
  thanked Mr. Okamoto. Director Barnes supplied additional information
  regarding the Summer Food Program. Director Barnes stated that North
  Park has been one of the sites for our Summer Food Program which is both
  funded and governed by the California Department of Education. A
  regulation of the State Department of Education is that a program cannot
  operate within a quarter mile of another site. This year, due to the pandemic,
  various school sites such as Centinela Elementary have been operating as
  Grab and Go breakfast and lunch sites. Our application for North Park was
  denied because North Park and Centinela Elementary School are very
  close in location – less than a quarter mile. Centinela Elementary School
  will be hosting the Summer Food Program. Signage will be provided at the
  North Park to inform youth of the new location. The Summer Food programs
  serves all youth, ages 18 and under, not just students of Centinela
  Elementary School. Similarly, the Inglewood Library application was also
  denied because Inglewood High School, located directly across the street,
  will be serving grab and go meals. We look forward to bringing back both

  5
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES June 3, 2021

  North Park and the Inglewood Library programs next summer assuming the
  pandemic is under control and the school sites are longer operating as a
  grab and go locations. Commissioner Beck asked if the Transportation
  Program a city funded program. Mr. Okamoto response was that the
  program is funding by the state and county.

Director Barnes stated that Geoffrey is responsible for the para-transit units which
provide curb to curb service. Seniors call, reserve a ride, and are taken to doctor’s
appointments, local shopping areas, and other places covered within the City’s
service area, Commissioner Beck stated in essence funding is provided by the
state and added he wants to understand how the Transportation Programs works
because it provides critical services to critical constituents which are the seniors.
Mr. Okamoto clarified the difference between the Access Program and the
Inglewood City Transportation Program. Access requires its participants to
physical go in and be interviewed in order to be considered eligible for the service.
The City’s Transportation Program simply requires an application to be completed,
proof of residency in the city and you be a senior.

Directors Report:

  Director Barnes gave an update on the following Capital Improvement Projects:

    Restroom Improvement Projects
    Parks Security Improvements
    Renovation of the Ballfields at Rogers Park
    Vincent Park Swimming Pool Resurfacing Project
    Renovation of the Ballfields at Darby Park and Lighting
    Improvements to Darby Park Infrastructure

Director Barnes referred to the 2015 preparation for the Measure ballot initiative
measure that was presented to California voters. The City participated in a
Countywide Park Needs Assessment. The City was tasked by the County with
identifying the top 10park projects that were in need of funding related to park
improvements. The projects were prioritized based on input from the community.
The City hosted a couple Park and Recreation Commission meetings where
residents were able to attend and give input on needed improvements ranging from
restroom room and playground equipment to security cameras and furniture.

We develop more than ten (10) projects. Director Barnes stated several projects
have been completed at various parks which include the Ballfield Renovation
Project for Darby Park (funded by the Los Angeles Dodgers Foundation), tennis
court improvements which were completed at all City parks including eight at

  6
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES June 3, 2021

Edward Vincent Park. Restroom improvements included one at Edward Vincent,
North and all at Center, Ashwood, Rogers and Simiski Parks. Five restrooms
remain to be renovated. That includes Edward Vincent, two at Darby and one at
Queen.

Security improvements have begun made through the installation of cameras at
Center, Ash wood, Rogers Simiski, and most recently, Darby Park which was
completed last month. Director Barnes stated that the next anticipated camera
project will be for Edward Vincent Park.

An additional project added to the list is to improve the picnic arbors located at
Edward Vincent Park near the Amphitheater and add shade structures at North
park. The North Park Project scope also included replacement of the woodchips
with a rubberized playground surfacing, rubberizing the track as opposed to the
decomposed granite and few other minor improvements. The final project added
to the list of improvements was added as a result of revisiting a proposed Queen
Park improvement Project in 2019. Director Barnes reiterated the number of
completed projects since 2015 and stated an opportunity has been presented to
have some of the future projects funded through Measure A, which was the
catalyst for the creation of the priority list.

Measure A was passed successfully by voters in 2016, funds were then made
available to us in 2018. As a City, we have been letting the money pool so we can
do a more substantial project. After being awarded the first sum of $250,000.00,
we allowed the money to rollover giving us a current balance of slightly over a
million dollars available. Restrooms remain a priority. Director Barnes stated that
once a priority list has been reestablished and is current, we would then submit
our application to Los Angeles County who over sees the Measure A funds to
request funding for the chosen projects.

For the upcoming budget, we will be requesting funding for one of the remaining
seven restrooms. Preference is to always use our grant funds and not utilize the
City’s general fund. Over the past few years, the City has had the luxury of
assisting with funding along with the use of grant funds.

Commissioner Denmon commented that the cameras at Darby Park are excellent.
Recreation Supervisor Mike Davis gave him a tour and identified the camera
locations. Chairman Denmon stated the camera positions, inability to be seen,
and coverage of the park are excellent. Commissioner Denmon asked what are
the procedures for funding smaller projects that do not meet the capital
improvement list criteria? Comissioner Denmon inquired about installing a
volleyball court at Darby Park. Director Barnes requested Commissioner Denmon

  7
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES June 3, 2021

email her and stated she will follow up with a discussion on his request. Director
Barnes stated smaller projects are also based upon funding availability.

  Public Comments

  None

  Commissioners Comments

  Commissioner Denmon wished everyone a wonderful summer and
stated he will see everyone in July.

  With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 6:46 p.m.
